ety.text: Borrowed from Latin American Spanish avocado, from the earlier aguacate, which comes from Classical Nahuatl āhuacatl (“avocado”). Doublet of abacate. Compare aguacatillo, avocadillo. The first mention can be found in a catalogue of Jamaican plants in 1696.

senses.d: The large, usually yellowish-green or black, savory fruit of the avocado tree.
The avocado tree, Persea americana, of the laurel family.
A dark chartreuse color, like the color of the skin of an avocado.
ex: It was exactly the same as my bathroom. Same cork floor, same avocado bathroom set.

From Middle English avoiden, from Anglo-Norman avoider, Old French esvuidier (“to empty out”), from es- + vuidier, from Vulgar Latin *vocitāre < Vulgar Latin *vocitum, ultimately related to Latin vacuus. Displaced native Old English forbūgan (literally “to bend away from”).

senses.d: To try not to meet or communicate with (a person); to shun.
To stay out of the way of (something harmful).
ex: One town was flooded from the storm, while the other town avoided the storm.

senses.d: To keep away from; to keep clear of; to stay away from.
ex: I try to avoid the company of gamblers.
What need a man foreſtall his date of griefe / And run to meet what he would moſt avoid?

senses.d: To try not to do something or to have something happen.
To make empty; to clear.
ex: If thou haue, he shal lyue with thee, and auoide thee out ; and he shal not sorewen vpon thee.

senses.d: To make void, to annul; to refute (especially a contract).
ex: […] how can those graunts of the Kings be avoyded, without wronging of those lords, which had those lands and lordships given them?

senses.d: To defeat or evade; to invalidate.
To emit or throw out; to void.
ex: […] a Toad piſſeth not, nor doe they containe thoſe urinary parts which are found in other animals, to avoid that ſerous excretion; […]

senses.d: To leave, evacuate; to leave as empty, to withdraw or come away from.
ex: Wherupon ſixe of vs onely ſtaied, and the reſt auoyded the Roome.

senses.d: To get rid of.
ex: […] expell out of your thoughts all douts, auoid out of your minds all feare; and like valiant champions aduance fooꝛth your ſtandards, […]
